cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: A cloudburst on the Spine. Every stream on the north bank is a torrent and the pound is up two marks in a night. The overflow weir is roaring and the east embankment is dark with seepage from end to end.

left.label: Every paddle open, now
left.outcome: Water thunders down the east flight. Lock 8 floods its towpath. The pound steadies.

right.label: Sandbag the embankment first
right.outcome: The town on the bank with sacks all night. The seepage slows. The pound does not.

cards.speaker: ilse
cards.text: The low street is under. Not cellars. Street. There are people on their roofs and the chapel undercroft's a well and the sandbags have gone down the flight with the rest. The moot's not meeting. The moot's bailing. Where's the Keeper?

left.label: On the paddles
left.outcome: You run every paddle yourself while Dace's men take boats to the roofs.

right.label: On a boat to the roofs
right.outcome: You pull eleven people off roofs. The pound does not fall. It waits for you.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The east embankment's got a boil in it the size of a barrel, below the chapel. Quenn says an hour, maybe two. And every hand I've got is on a roof or a paddle.

left.label: Every hand to the boil
left.outcome: Stone, timber, sacks, bodies. The boil stops. The roofs wait.

right.label: Cut the west bank into the Reach
right.outcome: The Reach floods to the gunwales. The east bank holds. The Hullfolk will not forget the choosing.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: The pound is coming in faster than rain can explain. The inflow at the north bank is a boil the size of a house. Whatever feeds the pound has opened up. Sorry. I don't know how to close it. I don't think anyone alive does.

left.label: Ask Vosk
left.outcome: "Noted." Vosk goes to the sluice house alone with the Company key. By morning the boil is smaller. She does not explain.

right.label: Drain the flight; buy time
right.outcome: Every paddle for three days. The lower pounds flood. The summit holds. Aldmere writes.

cards.speaker: hale
cards.text: The chapel is an island. The undercroft is full to the nave floor and the founding chest has floated up the steps and lies open in the aisle. Letters everywhere, wet. The town is coming for shelter and will read them.

left.label: Gather the letters; shelter the town
left.outcome: You and Hale gather letters in the dark while the town comes in. Some are read. Some are lost. The town hears a name: Marrow.

right.label: Shelter the town; let the letters go
right.outcome: The letters go down the aisle and out the door on the flood. Some reach the pound. Bram's people find them. He reads.

cards.speaker: stroud
cards.text: Two drowned on the low street. A lock hand and a child. I have laid them out at the inn. The town is not shouting. It is very quiet. In Year 44 it was quiet too, for about a day. Do something before the day is over.

left.label: Go to the inn and stand with them
left.outcome: You stand with the town at the laying-out. Nobody speaks to you. Nobody asks you to leave.

right.label: Drain the pound; nothing else matters
right.outcome: The paddles run for two days. The pound falls. The town buries its dead without you.

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: The pound has stopped rising. It has not started falling. The embankment holds, barely, with the whole town's timber in it. The rain has stopped. The north bank boil has not. Somewhere under the hill something is open that was shut.

left.label: Go to the sluice house tonight
left.outcome: Iron straps. A key you may or may not have. The sound of a river behind a door.

right.label: Hold the paddles open and wait
right.outcome: A week of open paddles. The pound falls a mark a day. The boil dwindles. Nobody explains it.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: The water is down. The low street is mud. In the Ledger there is a page for floods, in three Keepers' hands, and yours is the fourth. Every entry ends the same way: 'the pound was higher than the reservoirs could explain'.

left.label: Write the same
left.outcome: The fourth hand. The same sentence. Someone will read it.

right.label: Write what the town lost
right.outcome: Names. A cellar count. A child. The Ledger has never had names in it before.

cards.speaker: src_weather
cards.text: The gauge is at the third mark. Loaded barges cannot enter the chamber. The queue has become a camp. The Reach lies on its side in the mud. The aqueduct, for what it is worth, is running normally.

left.label: Close the summit to loaded vessels
left.outcome: Light boats only. Cargo is unloaded on the wharf and carried round by cart. The town hires out every horse it has.

right.label: One heavy boat at a time
right.outcome: One boat a watch, dragged over the sill by every hand. The sill loses stones. So does the town's patience.

cards.speaker: quenn
cards.text: The chamber floor's showing at the north corner. Nobody has seen it since Year 31. There's a grating in it, and under the grating, running water, going out, not in. Sorry. The pound has a drain and nobody knew.

left.label: Block the grating
left.outcome: Tamm makes a plug. The pound stops falling for two days. Then something under the hill pushes it out.

delayed_resources.message: The plug in the chamber grating has blown out.

right.label: Follow where the water goes
right.outcome: It goes north, under the bank, toward the sluice house. It always did.

cards.speaker: bram
cards.text: The Reach is aground. All of it. Old boats on their sides, families in the mud, the old singer in a tent. We have never asked the town for shelter. We ask the gate to ask for us, because we cannot make the words.

left.label: Ask the town
left.outcome: You ask Ilse. Ilse asks the moot. The moot, astonishing itself, says yes. Forty Hullfolk sleep in the town's lofts.

right.label: Open the Company warehouse
right.outcome: Forty Hullfolk in the Company's grain store. Pell finds out and cannot decide how to feel.

cards.speaker: src_gate
cards.text: A grain fleet has been in the camp nine days. Its master is selling grain to the town at a price it cannot pay, and to Sorrel bargees at one they can. The town is watching its bread go west across a dry pound.

left.label: Requisition the grain for the town
left.outcome: Emergency clause. The grain is the town's at a fair price. Aldmere protests. The town eats.

right.label: The master sells to whom he likes
right.outcome: The grain goes west by cart. The town watches. Ilse says nothing, loudly.

cards.speaker: vane
cards.text: Nine days. My principals have stopped writing letters and started writing lawyers. I've got a proposal: a Sorrel dredging crew, at Sorrel's cost, to cut the sill down a foot. The Company will never allow it. The Company is nine days away.

left.label: Let them cut the sill
left.outcome: Sorrel men with picks in the Company's lock chamber. The sill drops a foot. Heavy boats float. Vosk arrives on the tenth day and looks at the sill a long time.

right.label: Nobody cuts the Company's sill
right.outcome: "Then nobody's coal moves. Fine. I'll write to the lawyers myself."

cards.speaker: pell
cards.text: The Board has wired. It uses 'drought' four times and 'Keeper' five. It wishes to know why the reservoirs, 'ample by every report', have failed to sustain the pound. I do not know what to tell them. I have never not known.

left.label: Tell them the reservoirs never could
left.outcome: You write it plainly. Pell sends it, hand shaking. Ardent does not reply. Vosk does.

right.label: Tell them drought
right.outcome: You write 'drought'. Pell breathes. Ardent replies 'noted'. The pound falls a mark.

cards.speaker: dace
cards.text: Three things. The hands have been pumping the Reach end into the chamber by hand for six days. Two are down with their backs. And they've asked, since there's no boats, whether they're still lock hands or just men with buckets.

left.label: Still lock hands; full wages
left.outcome: Paid for pumping. They pump. The pound holds its mark for a week.

right.label: Send them home till the rain
right.outcome: Unpaid, home. The chamber dries. Two go down to Lock 6 and do not come back.

cards.speaker: src_ledger
cards.text: Rain, at last. The pound comes up a mark a day for a week. The camp breaks; the Reach floats. In the Ledger, the Year 31 entry ends: 'the pound recovered in a week, without rain'. Yours recovered with it. That is the only difference.

left.label: Note the difference
left.outcome: Without rain. Somebody in Year 31 wrote that and knew what it meant.

right.label: Note the recovery
right.outcome: The pound is back. The boats are back. You do not ask the water anything. This week.
